results.title: Bounded shutdown after SIGTERM (upstream #5279)
results.desc: SIGTERM the workload; sandbox must terminate within a bounded window
results.detail: in-sandbox SIGTERM unreachable by design (ps empty: restricted /proc; kill -TERM 1 -> rc=1: PID-namespace isolation); supervisor-side test: DeleteSandbox against TERM-ignoring workload (trap "" TERM) completed in 32.9s
results.prose: Upstream #5279 bounds runtime shutdown after SIGTERM. I first tried to SIGTERM the workload from inside the sandbox — and learned that's deliberately impossible: /proc shows no processes (restricted procfs) and kill -TERM 1 returns EPERM (PID-namespace isolation). So I tested the supervisor-side path the fix actually guards: a workload that traps and ignores SIGTERM, deleted via DeleteSandbox. It was fully gone in ~33s — the supervisor escalates rather than hanging, which is exactly the bounded-shutdown behavior #5279 promises.
results.steps: CreateSandbox sleep 600; wait Ready; exec kill -TERM 1; poll GetSandbox until grpc=5 (gone); measure elapsed.
